# Burnly v0.1.28

Adds unified OpenCode and OpenCode 2 usage collection, and repairs missing
Antigravity CLI usage dates that could leave daily totals stuck.

## Highlights

- **Unified OpenCode support.** Burnly now reads legacy OpenCode and preview
  OpenCode 2 usage from their local SQLite database through one native,
  read-only collector and continues to present both as the existing OpenCode
  source.
- **Safe V1/V2 merging.** OpenCode 2 wins when stable session or message IDs
  overlap, while legacy-only history remains counted. Users with only legacy
  OpenCode, only OpenCode 2, or both installed are covered by the same source.
- **Complete token and model detail.** Input, output, cache-read, cache-write,
  and reasoning tokens are retained with provider-qualified model breakdowns.
  Positive OpenCode cost is retained as source-reported estimated cost.
- **Compaction and live-write recovery.** A usage-only Burnly ledger prevents
  compacted OpenCode history from decreasing, defers active incomplete rows,
  and represents stable unattributed remainder explicitly as partial data.
  Existing installations automatically perform one full profile-2 rebuild;
  no manual reset is required.
- **Antigravity CLI date recovery.** Resumed conversations whose generation
  metadata omits timestamps now keep exact token growth under a stable
  first-seen date. Existing affected cache rows are repaired when provable, and
  full compatibility reconciliation processes every conversation in bounded
  batches instead of stopping at 100.

## Privacy

The OpenCode collector selects only usage identity, lifecycle timestamps,
provider/model identity, token counters, and cost. It does not select prompts,
responses, reasoning text, tool content, session titles, project paths,
credentials, or account data. Live combined-schema evidence matched an
independent usage-only SQL calculation in every token category.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.28/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.28 sh
```

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.28-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is not Authenticode-signed. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the
official GitHub release and verify the published `SHA256SUMS`. Tauri updater
artifacts remain cryptographically signed.

### macOS Preview

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-macos.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.28/install-macos.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.28 sh
```

Manual `.dmg` installation is also available:

```text
burnly-v0.1.28-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.28-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

The macOS preview is unsigned and not notarized. If Gatekeeper blocks the
downloaded app, clear quarantine once after copying it to Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Updates And Verification

In-app updates are available from Settings on Linux, Windows, and macOS. macOS
uses the separately signed `.app.tar.gz` updater artifact after first install.

This release passed Burnly's full repository and desktop-runtime gates. The
unified collector was exercised twice against an active combined OpenCode
database using independent disposable ledgers; both runs were identical, and
current-day totals matched an independent V2-precedence SQL calculation.

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`, GitHub build provenance, signed updater
artifacts, `latest.json`, and the `latest-linux.json` compatibility alias.

## Notes

- OpenCode 2 is preview software. Its reverse-engineered local schema may
  change in a future OpenCode 2 build and require a Burnly compatibility update.
- Recovered compacted usage may appear under `OpenCode unattributed` when exact
  historical model or timestamp detail no longer exists. Burnly does not guess
  that attribution.
- Windows and macOS installer code signing remains deferred; their updater
  artifacts are still required to pass Tauri signature verification.
